title: Thoracoscopic vs. open mammary artery harvesting in direct minimally invasive coronary bypass surgery – clinical and histomorphological examination
summary:
In minimally invasive heart bypass surgery (MIDCAB), there are different ways to remove the blood vessel needed for the bypass from inside the chest. This vessel can be harvested either through a small open incision or using a camera through very small cuts (thoracoscopic technique). So far, only few studies have directly compared these two minimally invasive methods, as most research has focused on comparing traditional open-heart surgery with minimally invasive approaches.

Due to recent technical advances, it is now possible to treat more than one blocked heart vessel through a small incision. For this, the chest wall artery must be harvested along its full length, which is often done using the camera-assisted technique. The aim of this study is to find out which method is better for patients, particularly in terms of pain after surgery, lung function, and the quality of the harvested blood vessel, in order to provide the safest and most gentle treatment possible.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1.    Patients with coronary heart disease
2.    Consent of the patient after detailed explanation of the study being conducted
3.    Patients with coronary heart disease and surgical findings that can be treated with minimally invasive bypass surgery
Exclusion criteria:
1.    Preoperative Forced Expiratory Volume in 1 Second  <1 liter 
2.    Body mass Index > 35
3.    Patient lacks capacity to give consent
